_comment: Each source carries: id, name, url, tier, verified, newest_seen. Tier 1 = primary institutional source (legislation, official press, court output). Tier 2 = supporting, national or journalistic. 'verified' means the endpoint was fetched by hand and returned a parseable feed. 'newest_seen' is the date of the newest item it held at that moment - because a feed can parse perfectly and still be dead. 'score_multiplier' down-weights sources that are useful but not authoritative. 'require_match' gates a source so only items matching the named topic list are ever scored - '@name' resolves to a shared list in rules.json's topic_gates. 'format' defaults to RSS/Atom; set it to 'wp-json' for a WordPress JSON API endpoint. 'score_multiplier' also marks paywalled sources down: they are tip-offs, never the cited source. Never mark a source verified you have not actually fetched.
_audit: 2026-09-02 - portfolio expanded to 30 entries, 25 enabled, then corrected against Actions run #14 rather than left on hand fetches. Added and confirmed working by the runner: Financial Times EU section (25 items, same-day), ECFR (25, 1 day), CEPS via the new wp-json adapter (30, same-day), Der Spiegel International (20, 1 day), RTE News (20, same-day), France 24 Europe (30, same-day). Two candidates failed at the runner and are recorded rather than hidden: Bruegel returns 403 to GitHub's runners though it serves a browser fine, so it is disabled like Euractiv; and Deutsche Welle's Europe feed is RSS 1.0 (RDF), which this parser does not read, so it collected nothing and France 24 took its place. Three more were asked for and do not exist as feeds: the European Policy Centre serves its single-page app for every candidate path, the EEAS publishes no RSS anywhere so the EU Delegation to the United Kingdom cannot be monitored this way, and the Commission's Midday Express has no feed of its own - its items already arrive through ec-presscorner, whose type parameter the API ignores. Five entries are deliberately disabled and documented: the three European Parliament feeds return an empty response to GitHub's runners, Euractiv 403s them, and now Bruegel does too. Previous audit 2026-08-31 (20 entries, corrected against run #8). The run health table is the authority, not a hand fetch.

sources.name: European Commission - press corner
sources.note: Live, same-day. Do NOT add a pagesize parameter: it silently breaks the newest-first ordering and the feed starts returning month-old items while still parsing perfectly. That is what made this look dead through August.

sources.name: European Parliament - press releases
sources.note: DISABLED 31 Aug 2026. europarl.europa.eu returns an empty response (0 bytes) to GitHub's runners - not a parsing problem, an access one. Kept in the file, switched off, so the Parliament gap stays visible instead of failing every run. Re-enable and run a health check if you ever move collection off GitHub Actions.

sources.name: European Parliament - committee press releases
sources.note: DISABLED 31 Aug 2026. Same block as ep-press: empty response from GitHub's runners. Editorially this is the feed worth fighting for - committee stage is where a law's wording actually changes - so re-test it first if collection ever moves off Actions.

sources.name: European Parliament - texts adopted
sources.note: DISABLED 31 Aug 2026. Same block as ep-press. EUR-Lex partly covers the same ground: adopted texts reach the Official Journal feed eventually.

sources.name: Council of the EU - press releases
sources.note: Live and current: run #8 saw 20 items, newest 2 days old. It carries its timestamp in an Atom-namespaced <a10:updated> tag rather than <pubDate>, which collect.py has handled since the 26 Aug parser fix.

sources.name: EUR-Lex - Commission proposals
sources.note: The healthiest EUR-Lex feed and the one that matters most: proposals are where a law starts. Titles are CELEX identifiers with truncated descriptions, so keyword scoring on the title under-performs - hence the multiplier. Slow to respond, hence the raised timeout.

sources.name: EUR-Lex - case law
sources.note: The only route to Court of Justice output in this set - the Court's own site publishes no usable RSS (checked 31 Aug 2026). Roughly a third of its items carry no readable item-level date, so date_fallback is set to 'channel'.

sources.name: EUR-Lex - Official Journal L (acts in force)
sources.note: Law as published. Batch feed, so it arrives in lumps rather than steadily. Same CELEX title problem as the proposals feed.

sources.name: European Central Bank - press
sources.note: Live and current. Rates, supervision and the digital euro - the money-and-work beat leans on this.

sources.name: gov.uk - news and communications
sources.note: Live, very high volume, all of Whitehall. The workhorse of the UK side. The noise list in rules.json does the real filtering; add a keywords parameter to narrow at source if it ever overwhelms a run.

sources.name: House of Commons Library - research briefings
sources.note: Added 31 Aug 2026. Impartial explanatory briefings written for non-specialists, which is the closest thing in the set to what Passerelle itself is trying to be. Frequently covers UK-EU divergence directly.

sources.name: UK Parliament - all bills
sources.note: Live. Dates live in <a10:updated>, not <pubDate>. High volume on a first run - expect the whole live bill list at once, then only movements.

sources.name: gov.uk - Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office
sources.note: Live, but roughly nine in ten items are travel advice and consular guidance. The noise list kills those; without it this feed alone would dominate the digest.

sources.name: gov.uk - Department for Business and Trade
sources.note: The best divergence source in the set - UKCA/CE marking, trade remedies, market access. Consider promoting to tier 1.

sources.name: UK in a Changing Europe
sources.note: Added 31 Aug 2026. ESRC-funded academic initiative writing about nothing except the UK-EU relationship, non-partisan and readable. The closest fit to this project's subject of any source here.

sources.name: Centre for European Reform
sources.note: Added 31 Aug 2026. Pro-European reformist think tank, London and Brussels. Useful for the argument behind a development rather than the fact of it - treat as context, not as a primary claim.

sources.name: EUobserver
sources.note: Verified 31 Aug 2026. Independent Brussels newsroom, strong on institutional accountability. Journalism, not a primary source - always follow it back to the document.

sources.name: Politico Europe
sources.note: Fast and well sourced on Brussels process. Same rule as EUobserver: it tells you something is happening, the document tells you what.

sources.name: Euractiv
sources.note: DISABLED 31 Aug 2026. Returns HTTP 403 to GitHub's runners, though it serves a browser fine - the runner IP range is blocked. Nothing to fix at this end.

sources.name: Euronews - My Europe
sources.note: Added 31 Aug 2026. The European-politics vertical specifically, not the general news feed. Broadest and most general of the media sources, hence the lowest multiplier - useful mainly for spotting what has broken through to a mainstream audience.

sources.name: Financial Times — European Union
sources.note: FT's European Union section feed. Verified by hand 2026-09-02: 25 items, newest same-day. PAYWALLED - headlines and standfirsts come through in full, the articles do not. Treat it as a tip-off feed only. Never cite the FT as the source in a Passerelle piece; go and find the primary document it is reporting on. The section is already EU-scoped, so no topic gate is applied.

sources.name: Bruegel
sources.note: DISABLED 2 Sep 2026. Bruegel serves a browser perfectly (verified by hand the same day: valid RSS, 10 items) but returns HTTP 403 to GitHub's runners, exactly as Euractiv does. An access block at the far end, not a fault here. Kept in the file, switched off, so the gap stays visible instead of being forgotten. Worth re-testing every few months.

sources.name: European Council on Foreign Relations
sources.note: European foreign and security policy think tank. Verified by hand 2026-09-02: valid RSS; Actions run #14 the same day collected 25 items, newest 1 day old. Open access. No topic gate: European policy is ECFR's whole remit.

sources.name: Centre for European Policy Studies
sources.note: CEPS has switched its RSS off at the server - every /feed path returns a WordPress error - but its WordPress JSON API is open and current. Read through the wp-json adapter in collect.py rather than the RSS parser, which is what format: wp-json selects. Verified by hand 2026-09-02: 200 OK, newest post same-day. Open access. No topic gate: CEPS only writes about EU policy. Confirmed working in Actions run #14: 30 items, newest same-day, collected through the adapter.

sources.name: Der Spiegel — International
sources.note: German national paper, English-language international desk. Verified by hand 2026-09-02: valid RSS, 20 items, newest 1 day old. Gated to EU topics, because the desk covers the whole world. PARTLY PAYWALLED - use as a tip-off, cite the primary document.

sources.name: RTÉ News
sources.note: Ireland's public broadcaster. Verified by hand 2026-09-02: valid RSS, 20 items, newest same-day. General Irish news, so the EU topic gate does the heavy lifting. Free to read. Ireland is the member state with the sharpest read on UK-EU questions, which is why it is the Irish feed and not another. Note the path: /rss/news.xml works, /rss/world.xml and /feeds/rss/ are both 404.

sources.name: France 24 — Europe
sources.note: France's public international broadcaster, Europe desk, in English. Verified by hand 2026-09-02: valid RSS 2.0, 30 items, newest same-day. Free to read, which is the point of having it next to the paywalled two. Gated to EU topics. It is here in place of Deutsche Welle's Europe feed, which is live and current but published as RSS 1.0 (RDF) - a format this parser does not read, so it collected zero items in Actions run #14.

sources.name: YouGov UK
sources.note: Added 31 Aug 2026. GATED. YouGov publishes around a hundred items a fortnight and almost none of them are about Europe - the newest item when this was added was about Grand Theft Auto VI. require_match drops everything that does not mention EU politics before it reaches scoring. Polling is evidence about opinion, not a development: use it to support a story, not as one.

sources.name: Ipsos UK
sources.note: Added 31 Aug 2026. GATED, same reasoning as yougov-uk. Ipsos ran the 2016 Perils of Perception work on EU misperceptions, which is the evidence base this publication was argued from.

sources.name: Pew Research Center
sources.note: Added 31 Aug 2026. GATED. Mostly US domestic research, but its Global Attitudes surveys cover European opinion and are among the few genuinely cross-national sources. High volume, so the gate matters more here than anywhere.
